Updated 2026-07-04 after NCBI re-probe. NCBI Assembly search for "Dunaliella bardawil" was auto-translated to "Dunaliella salina" (taxid 3046), indicating NCBI treats D. bardawil as a taxonomic synonym of D. salina. The two assemblies returned (GCA_002284615.2 v2 and GCA_002284615.1 v1) are both for D. salina strain CCAP 19/18, already in yes.tsv as Dunaliella salina SA134. No independent D. bardawil genome exists on NCBI as a distinct taxon. To promote: requires accepting D. salina synonymy, which conflicts with phenotype-backed strain identity. Retain in hold pending taxonomic clarification.

Added 2026-07-06. Chlamydomonas sp. ICE-L is an Antarctic sea ice green alga isolated from floating sea ice near Zhongshan Station, Antarctica during the Chinese 18th Antarctic Science Exploration (2001-2002). He et al. 2019 (PMC6689313) explicitly states cultures were grown at 5°C — explicit strain-resolved culture temperature, well below the <=15°C psychrophilic threshold. SEQUENCE BLOCKER: NCBI Assembly GCA_013435795.1 (ASM1343579v1, Scaffold, 466x coverage, Nanjing Normal University 2020; BioProject PRJNA636631; taxid 309537) exists and is current, but the FTP directory has no protein.faa.gz file and the assembly API response shows no annotation_info — no protein annotation is available from NCBI. To promote to yes.tsv: verify that a protein FASTA becomes available (e.g., via a future NCBI annotation run or an external annotation deposited by the authors), or run gene prediction on the nucleotide FASTA (e.g., Braker2/Augustus/MAKER). Phenotype evidence is strong once sequence side is resolved.
